document_type: technical blog post with measurements and code
reader_and_goal: ML practitioners who will copy the five changes and repeat the explanations

segments.title: Title, TL;DR, summary chart and baseline setup (pages 1 to 3)
passages: 5 Lines of Code to Make Your LLM
segments.why_this_budget: Sets the headline claim and the measurement method everything else depends on.
checks: Headline 3x and '250 ms to 80 ms' arithmetic; 'five one-line changes' against the code actually shown
Hardware line 'one RTX 5070 (8 GB)' and software versions
Reproducibility: batch size, sequence length, number of steps or runs, warm-up, variance
The timing code: what is inside the timed region, clock used, synchronisation
'on-par performance with same compute budget' and other TL;DR wording against what is measured
Dataset figures: Tiny Shakespeare 1M characters, ~338k tokens

segments.title: Optimizations 1 and 2: TF32 and bfloat16 autocast (pages 3 to 7)
passages: TF32: a cheaper multiply, same float32 tensors
bfloat16 autocast: half the bytes per activation
segments.why_this_budget: Dense hardware and numerics claims, and the post's central diagnosis ('memory bound') is derived here.
checks: TF32 bit layout, where it applies, and which GPUs support it
The code comment mapping 'highest', 'high', 'medium' to float32, TF32, bfloat16
A100 datasheet figures 19.5 and 156 TFLOPS and the '8x ceiling'
The inference from 1.43x to 'memory bound', the '60%' utilisation claim, and 'expect 1.5-3x' against the post's own 1.43x
bfloat16 vs float16: bit layouts, range, GradScaler; what autocast keeps in float32; what dtype logits and loss have
Whether the explanation for the small autocast gain is supported by the measurements

passages: Padding the vocabulary: Nice numbers for

checks: 50257, 50304, 'nearest multiple of 128', 47 extra tokens, divisibility claims
The GPTconfig listing against the setup and the rest of the post (block_size, names)

segments.title: global-consistency
segments.why_this_budget: The same numbers and claims recur in the summary chart, sections, table and conclusion.
checks: Every ms figure and ratio wherever it appears: TL;DR chart, section 'MEASURED' boxes, table, waterfall, prose
Percent wording ('6%', '10% faster', '3x') against a consistent definition
One-line descriptions on pages 1 to 2 against the detailed sections (do they say the same thing)
Sequence length, vocabulary size, model size, hardware wherever stated or implied
Claims repeated in 'USE IT WHEN', 'LIMITATIONS' and conclusions that contradict each other
Terms used with more than one meaning (kernel, memory, on-chip, precision)

segments.title: copy-consistency
checks: Typos and grammar
Capitalisation and naming of products, classes and terms
Number, unit and symbol formats (x vs ×, ms spacing, thousands separators)
Code identifiers consistent between listings and prose
Parallel structure of repeated blocks and glossary coverage

NVIDIA A100 datasheet: FP32 and TF32 peak TFLOPS; memory bandwidth
PyTorch autocast op lists: which ops autocast to float32; whether documented
Karpathy 'Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)': ms per step at each stage, vocab padding gain
GPT-2 XL head count; GPT-2 context length; Tiny Shakespeare token count
